headline: Customers can now apply partner coupons to orders, but one "single-use" $100 coupon can be used several times by sending quick repeat requests.
what_changed: Adds a new web address the app answers so a coupon code can be applied to a ticket order.
The app looks up the code, checks it hasn't been used, takes its amount off the order, then marks the coupon as used.
Codes are tidied before checking: extra spaces are removed and letters are made uppercase, so typing "vip100" works like "VIP100".
If anything goes wrong, the customer sees a short error message, such as "coupon not found" or "already used".

risks.title: A single-use $100 coupon can be redeemed several times
risks.explanation: The app first checks whether the coupon is used, then gives the discount, and only then marks the coupon as used. These are separate steps with nothing locking them together. If the same code is sent twice at almost the same moment (a double-click, or a simple script), both requests pass the check, and each takes another $100 off. A coupon could also go onto several different orders. Partners hand out $100 VIP coupons, so this is real money and easy to abuse. Ask the developer to make the check and the 'mark as used' one single step, so only the first request can succeed.

risks.title: Discount can exceed the ticket price
risks.explanation: Nothing checks that the discount is smaller than the order total. If a $100 coupon goes on a $40 order, the amount to pay becomes minus $60. Together with the repeat-use problem above, discounts on one order can keep stacking. Depending on how checkout treats a negative amount, this could mean free tickets or confusing refunds. Ask the developer to cap the discount at the order total.

risks.title: Anyone can apply a coupon to any order
risks.explanation: The new web address doesn't check who is asking or whether the order belongs to them. Someone holding a code could put it on a stranger's order. Also, a typo in the order number still marks the coupon as used, even though no order got the discount. The VIP guest then finds their coupon already spent. Ask the developer to confirm the order exists and belongs to the person applying the coupon.

risks.title: A half-finished redemption can leave things out of step
risks.explanation: The discount and the 'mark as used' are saved as two separate changes, not one all-or-nothing change. If the second change fails, the order keeps the discount but the coupon stays unused and can be used again. This is rare, but the fix for the first risk should cover it too.

questions_for_developer: If the same coupon code is sent twice at the same moment, can both requests get the discount? Can you make the 'is it used?' check and the 'mark it used' step happen as one locked step?
What happens when a $100 coupon goes on an order that costs less than $100? Can we stop the amount to pay from going below zero?
Who is allowed to apply a coupon to an order? Can you check that the order exists and belongs to the logged-in customer before using up the coupon?
Can one order receive more than one coupon? Is that what we want?
good_news: The change is small and limited to the new coupon feature. The existing pay step is unchanged.
Coupon codes and order numbers are kept separate from the database instructions. So the classic trick of slipping commands in through a typed code doesn't work here.
Codes are tidied up first (spaces removed, letters made uppercase), so customers are less likely to be rejected over a typo.
